how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit the running configuration for Type 0 (cleartext) and Type 7 (reversibly obfuscated) passwords as well as plaintext routing authentication keys. Type 7 is considered plaintext-equivalent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines containing 'password 0 <text>', 'password 7 <hash>' (reversible), or unencrypted key strings indicate plaintext credentials. Lines with 'secret 9' or 'secret 8' indicate properly encrypted secrets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve and inspect configuration backup files from TFTP, FTP, SCP repositories, or network management platforms for plaintext credential types using pattern matching.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Matches reveal plaintext or Type 7 credentials. Categorize by type: lines with 'neighbor X.X.X.X password' = bgp_md5_key; 'area X authentication-key' = ospf_key; 'snmp-server community' = snmp_community_string; 'enable password' = management_password.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS/IOS-XE, specifically check whether 'service password-encryption' is enabled (which applies Type 7 to stored passwords) and whether stronger encryption (Type 8/9) has been applied to privileged-level secrets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'service password-encryption' present means Type 7 is applied but this is reversible and should be treated as plaintext. 'enable secret 9' or 'enable secret 8' indicates strong encryption. Absence of 'service password-encryption' with plain 'enable password' entries is a clear finding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check BGP neighbor configurations for plaintext MD5 passwords and OSPF/EIGRP interface authentication key configurations.
how_to_obtain.command: show running-config | section (router bgp|router ospf|router eigrp)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BGP lines with 'neighbor X.X.X.X password <text>' or OSPF lines with 'ip ospf authentication-key <text>' (not encrypted) confirm routing protocol keys stored in plaintext. EIGRP 'authentication key-chain' with plaintext key strings is also a finding.

typical_values: ["management_password"]
["snmp_community_string", "management_password"]
["bgp_md5_key", "ospf_key", "management_password", "snmp_community_string"]

option_description: Controls whether all credentials stored in router configuration files are protected by strong, irreversible encryption. Covers enable passwords, line passwords, SNMP community strings, and routing protocol keys.
security_impact: The Rego rule hardcoded_routing_credentials_in_config fires when credential_storage_encrypted is false, triggering a medium-criticality exposure. Plaintext credentials in config files are directly exploitable via T1552.001 (Credentials In Files) and T1602.002 (Network Device Configuration Dump). Any user with file read access to the running config or a backup can extract credentials immediately.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, display the running configuration and grep for password-related lines to identify plaintext or weakly encrypted credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines showing 'secret 9' or 'secret 8' indicate strong encryption. Lines showing 'password 7' indicate weak reversible encryption. Lines showing 'password 0' or bare passwords indicate plaintext.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify whether service password-encryption is globally enabled on Cisco IOS.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of 'service password-encryption' indicates type 7 encoding is applied, but this is weak. Absence means plaintext. Strong posture requires type 8 or type 9 hashes via 'enable secret' or 'username secret'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux-based routers such as those running FRRouting, inspect the daemon configuration files for plaintext credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Credentials should not appear as recognizable plaintext strings. If readable words appear adjacent to password keywords, the attribute should be set to false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS-XE, check the authentication type indicators for all local user accounts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each username line should show 'secret 9' (scrypt) or 'secret 8' (PBKDF2). Any entry showing 'password' or 'secret 5' (MD5) fails the strong encryption requirement.

typical_values: false (common in legacy deployments using service password-encryption with type 7)
true (hardened deployments using type 8 or type 9 secrets exclusively)

option_description: Controls whether the router accepts and forwards IP packets that carry Loose Source Routing (LSR) or Strict Source Routing (SSR) options in the IP header, allowing the sender to dictate the forwarding path.
security_impact: The Rego rule ip_source_routing_enabled fires when this is true and acl_blocks_source_routed_packets is false, or when source_routing_scope is 'all'. This creates a low-criticality exposure mapped to T1599 (Network Boundary Bridging) and T1090.003 (Multi-hop Proxy). Source routing allows attackers to bypass firewall and routing policy controls by forcing packets through specific hops.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS or IOS-XE, check the global configuration for the source-route command.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Absence of any output means source routing is enabled by default on older IOS. The string 'no ip source-route' confirms it is disabled. Set attribute to false only when 'no ip source-route' is present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux-based routers, query the kernel parameter for each interface and the global default.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All values should return 0 to confirm source routing is disabled. Any interface showing value 1 means source routing is accepted on that interface and the attribute should be set to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, verify the persistent sysctl configuration to ensure source routing is disabled across reboots.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entries such as 'net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route=0' and 'net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route=0' confirm the setting is persistently disabled.

typical_values: false (hardened deployments with 'no ip source-route' applied)
true (default on older Cisco IOS versions prior to 12.3 without explicit hardening)

option_description: Defines the scope of interfaces on which the router accepts source-routed packets. Possible values are 'none' (disabled everywhere), 'external_only' (only on interfaces facing untrusted networks), or 'all' (accepted on every interface).
security_impact: The Rego rule ip_source_routing_enabled additionally triggers when source_routing_scope is 'all' combined with ip_source_routing_enabled being true. A scope of 'all' is the most dangerous configuration because it allows source-routed packets to traverse even internal trusted segments, amplifying T1599 (Network Boundary Bridging) risk across the entire routing domain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, identify all interfaces and determine whether source routing is enabled globally or per-interface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If 'no ip source-route' appears globally and no interface overrides exist, scope is 'none'. If only external-facing interfaces lack the command, scope is 'external_only'. If the command is absent globally and on all interfaces, scope is 'all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, enumerate accept_source_route for every interface to determine which interfaces accept source routing.
how_to_obtain.command: for iface in $(ls /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/); do echo "$iface: $(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/$iface/accept_source_route)"; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All interfaces returning 0 maps to 'none'. Only external interfaces returning 1 maps to 'external_only'. Multiple or all interfaces returning 1 maps to 'all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the network interface inventory documentation to map interface names to their roles, then cross-reference with the accept_source_route values obtained from the device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A complete mapping of interface role to source routing acceptance. If any internal interfaces accept source routing, scope should be recorded as 'all' regardless of intent.

typical_values: none (hardened configuration, recommended)
all (default on many unhardenened IOS and Linux deployments)
external_only (partial hardening, uncommon but observed in some perimeter designs)

option_description: Indicates whether an ACL is configured to explicitly drop packets carrying IP source routing options, functioning as a compensating control when the global source routing disable command is not available or not applied.
security_impact: The Rego rule ip_source_routing_enabled checks this attribute as a compensating control. When ip_source_routing_enabled is true but acl_blocks_source_routed_packets is also true, the rule does not fire because the ACL provides an equivalent mitigation. Without this ACL and with source routing enabled, the exposure to T1599 and T1090.003 is unmitigated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, search all ACLs for rules matching IP options, specifically LSR and SSR option keywords.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing 'deny ip any any option lsr' or 'deny ip any any option record-route' or similar option-matching deny entries confirms ACL coverage. No output means no ACL is blocking source-routed packets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Display the full running configuration and inspect ACLs for source routing option deny rules.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACL entries with 'option lsr' or 'option ssrr' in deny statements confirm the compensating control is present. Verify the ACL is also applied to relevant interfaces with 'ip access-group' statements.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux using iptables, check for rules matching IP options byte patterns that correspond to source routing.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A DROP rule matching IP option type 131 (LSR) or 137 (SSR) confirms the compensating ACL is in place. If nftables is used, run 'nft list ruleset' and inspect for ip option lsr or ssrr matching rules.

typical_values: false (most deployments rely on the global disable command rather than an explicit ACL)
true (defense-in-depth configurations or environments where global disable is not supported)

option_description: Controls whether the router's interfaces accept and process incoming ICMP redirect messages, which can instruct the router to change its routing table to send traffic for a destination through a different next-hop gateway.
security_impact: The Rego rule icmp_redirect_messages_enabled fires when this is true and either the interface role is 'external' or 'dmz', or when secure_redirects_enabled is false. This creates a low-criticality exposure tied to T1557 (Adversary-in-the-Middle) and T1090.003 (Multi-hop Proxy). An attacker on a connected subnet can spoof ICMP redirects to silently reroute victim traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, check each interface configuration for the 'no ip redirects' command.
how_to_obtain.command: show running-config | section interface | include interface|ip redirects
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Interfaces showing 'no ip redirects' have redirects disabled. Interfaces where this line is absent have redirects enabled by default. At least one interface without 'no ip redirects' means attribute is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, query the ICMP redirect acceptance setting for all interfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Values of 0 for all interfaces indicate redirects are disabled. Any interface showing value 1 means ICMP redirects are accepted and the attribute should be set to true for that interface's context.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS-XE, use the show interfaces command to confirm ICMP redirect status per interface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing 'ICMP redirects are never sent' or 'ICMP redirects are not sent' per interface indicates disabled status. 'ICMP redirects are always sent' indicates enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, verify the persistent sysctl configuration for redirect acceptance settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines such as 'net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=0' confirm persistent disabling. Missing entries mean the kernel default applies, which is typically 1 (enabled) for hosts and variable for routers.

typical_values: true (default on most platforms without explicit hardening)
false (hardened configurations following CIS benchmarks or vendor hardening guides)

option_description: Classifies the functional role of a routing interface to indicate whether it faces external untrusted networks, a DMZ, internal trusted segments, or is used exclusively for device management. This role context is used to apply risk-appropriate security policies.
security_impact: The Rego rule icmp_redirect_messages_enabled uses interface_role to determine severity. When icmp_redirects_enabled is true and interface_role is 'external' or 'dmz', the exposure fires unconditionally regardless of secure_redirects_enabled. External and DMZ interfaces carry the highest risk because they are reachable by untrusted parties who can forge ICMP redirects without requiring access to internal segments.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review network topology documentation and interface naming conventions to map each interface to its functional role. Common conventions include naming interfaces with prefixes like ext, wan, dmz, int, or mgmt.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented mapping of interface name to role classification. Interfaces connected to ISP uplinks or untrusted peering are 'external'. Interfaces connecting to server DMZ segments are 'dmz'. Interfaces connecting to internal LAN segments are 'internal'. Out-of-band management interfaces are 'management'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List all interfaces with their IP addresses and descriptions to assist with role identification.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Interface descriptions should indicate connected segment purpose. Cross-reference IP subnets with network documentation to confirm role assignments.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, display full interface configurations including descriptions and IP addresses.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each interface block with a description field and IP address. Interfaces with RFC1918 addresses connected to internal subnets are typically 'internal'. Interfaces with public IP addresses or direct ISP connections are 'external'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Cisco DNA Center or similar network management platforms, navigate to the device inventory, select the router, and view the interface topology map to confirm each interface's network segment role.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cisco DNA Center > Inventory > Device Detail > Interfaces > Topology View
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Visual confirmation of each interface's connected network segment and its classification as external, DMZ, internal, or management.

typical_values: external (WAN or ISP-facing interfaces)
internal (LAN-facing interfaces connecting to trusted segments)
dmz (interfaces connecting to demilitarized zones hosting public-facing services)
management (out-of-band management interfaces)

option_description: Controls whether the router interface restricts ICMP redirect acceptance to only those redirects originating from gateways already present in the routing table, rather than accepting redirects from any host on the connected subnet.
security_impact: The Rego rule icmp_redirect_messages_enabled fires when icmp_redirects_enabled is true and secure_redirects_enabled is false, regardless of interface role. This provides a partial mitigation path: if ICMP redirects cannot be fully disabled, accepting only gateway-sourced redirects reduces but does not eliminate the T1557 (Adversary-in-the-Middle) risk. An attacker who has compromised a gateway can still inject redirects, so full disabling is preferred.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, query the secure_redirects kernel parameter for each interface and the global setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A value of 1 for an interface indicates only gateway-originated redirects are accepted (secure redirects enabled). A value of 0 means redirects from any host are accepted. On Cisco IOS, this concept does not exist as a distinct setting, so secure_redirects_enabled should be set to false for IOS devices.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the persistent sysctl configuration files for the secure_redirects parameter setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An entry 'net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects=1' confirms the setting is persistently enabled. Absence of this setting means the default applies, which is typically 1 on Linux but should be explicitly confirmed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Directly read the kernel proc filesystem value for the specific interface of interest.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output of '1' confirms secure redirects are enabled for this interface. Replace 'eth0' with the actual interface name. For Cisco IOS and similar platforms that lack this distinction, document as false.

typical_values: true (Linux default, only gateway-originated ICMP redirects accepted)
false (explicitly disabled or not applicable on Cisco IOS and similar platforms)

option_description: Controls whether the router is configured to authenticate NTP time sources using cryptographic keys, validating that time synchronization updates originate from trusted and legitimate NTP servers rather than spoofed or rogue sources.
security_impact: The Rego rule ntp_unauthenticated_synchronization fires when ntp_servers_configured is true and ntp_authentication_enabled is false, creating a low-criticality exposure tied to T1557 (Adversary-in-the-Middle) and T1124 (System Time Discovery). Unauthenticated NTP allows attackers to perform NTP spoofing attacks that manipulate system time, which can invalidate TLS certificate windows, corrupt log timestamps critical for forensics, and disrupt time-sensitive routing protocol operations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, display the NTP configuration including authentication keys and trusted key assignments.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A correctly configured output should contain 'ntp authenticate', one or more 'ntp authentication-key' lines defining key IDs and hashes, and 'ntp trusted-key' entries. All three elements must be present. Absence of 'ntp authenticate' or missing trusted-key assignments means authentication is not fully enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS, verify NTP authentication status and the association with configured servers using the show ntp command.
how_to_obtain.command: show ntp associations detail | include authenticated|auth
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing 'authenticated' for each NTP server association confirms authentication is active and working. Associations showing 'unauthenticated' indicate that despite configuration, authentication may not be functioning correctly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux systems using chrony, check the chrony configuration for key file references and server authentication directives.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A 'keyfile' directive pointing to a valid key file and server lines containing a 'key' parameter confirm NTP authentication is configured. If using ntpd instead of chrony, check 'grep -E "trustedkey|requestkey|keys" /etc/ntp.conf'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux using ntpd, verify the ntp.conf for authentication configuration and confirm keys are loaded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of a 'keys' file directive and 'trustedkey' entries listing key IDs confirms NTP authentication is configured. Cross-reference with 'ntpq -p' to verify server associations are actually using the keys.

typical_values: false (most enterprise router deployments do not configure NTP authentication)
true (hardened deployments following DISA STIG or CIS benchmark requirements)

option_description: Controls whether one or more NTP servers are explicitly defined on the router, causing the device to actively synchronize its system clock against those time sources. Without NTP server definitions, the router relies on its internal hardware clock, which drifts over time and cannot be validated against a trusted authority.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'ntp_unauthenticated_synchronization' evaluates this attribute as the primary gate: if 'ntp_servers_configured' is true, the policy then checks whether NTP authentication is also enabled. A router with NTP servers defined but without authentication (ntp_authentication_enabled false) is flagged for the 'Ntp Unauthenticated Synchronization' exposure, which enables clock manipulation attacks that corrupt log timestamps, invalidate certificate validity windows, and disrupt time-sensitive routing protocol operations. Conversely, if no NTP servers are configured at all, the router is not actively synchronizing, which also undermines log integrity and certificate checking but does not trigger this specific rule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS/IOS-XE, display all NTP configuration including any defined server or peer addresses.
how_to_obtain.command: show ntp status && show running-config | include ntp server
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more lines such as 'ntp server 10.0.0.1' or 'ntp server pool.ntp.org' indicate ntp_servers_configured = true. If no 'ntp server' lines appear, the value is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Juniper JunOS, inspect the NTP configuration stanza within the running configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing 'server <IP or hostname>' entries confirms NTP servers are configured. An empty or missing stanza indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the stored startup or running configuration file exported from the router, searching for NTP server directives applicable to the platform vendor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Grep for 'ntp server' (Cisco), 'server' within the 'system ntp' block (Juniper), or 'ntp-server' (Huawei). Presence of at least one match confirms the attribute is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the router via RESTCONF or a network management platform API to retrieve NTP configuration state programmatically.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON response containing 'reference-time' or 'server-address' fields populated with valid NTP server addresses confirms ntp_servers_configured = true.

typical_values: true (most managed enterprise and ISP routers have at least one NTP server defined)
false (common on unconfigured, legacy, or isolated routers that have never had a hardening baseline applied)

option_description: Controls whether an NTP access-group (Cisco) or equivalent platform ACL is applied to the router's NTP service, restricting which source IP addresses or peers are permitted to query, synchronize with, or act as a peer to the router's NTP process. Without this restriction, any host can interact with the router's NTP daemon, including submitting time updates that could manipulate the clock.
security_impact: The Rego policy includes a compound condition where 'ntp_servers_configured == true' AND 'ntp_authentication_enabled' is false AND 'ntp_access_group_configured' is false together reinforce the 'Ntp Unauthenticated Synchronization' finding. Even if NTP authentication is absent, having an access group reduces the attack surface by limiting which hosts can send NTP traffic to the router. An absent access group means any attacker-reachable host can attempt NTP spoofing or amplification attacks using the router as a reflector, or inject crafted NTP responses to shift the router's clock, corrupting log timestamps and disrupting RPKI, BGP timer calculations, or certificate-based authentication.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS/IOS-XE, display the NTP configuration section and look for access-group statements that define trusted NTP query and peer sources.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines such as 'ntp access-group peer 10', 'ntp access-group serve-only 20', or 'ntp access-group query-only 30' confirm the attribute is true. Absence of any 'ntp access-group' line means false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Juniper JunOS, check whether restrict or allow statements are defined within the NTP configuration stanza to control peer access.
how_to_obtain.command: show configuration system ntp | display set | match restrict
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing 'set system ntp restrict <network>' statements confirms an NTP access restriction is in place (true). No matching output indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the exported router configuration for NTP access-group or equivalent directives paired with their referenced ACL definitions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one matching line confirms ntp_access_group_configured = true. Zero matches means the attribute is false and the NTP service is unrestricted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an untrusted host outside the expected NTP peer range, attempt an NTP query against the router's management or loopback IP to verify whether the access restriction drops or responds to the request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If the access group is correctly configured, the query should time out or be refused. A successful time response from an unauthorized source indicates ntp_access_group_configured is effectively false or misconfigured.

typical_values: false (the majority of routers in real deployments do not configure NTP access groups, leaving the service open)
true (found on hardened devices following CIS Cisco IOS benchmarks or NIST SP 800-54 guidance)
